Prove the plugin architecture end to end: a user adds an Intimacy Dossier page to a character, edits a field in the lazily loaded editor, and the value survives a reload. The whole schema half of the Intimacy type ships here, because the load boundary validates every page against it.

Purpose: CHAR-04 (add) and INTM-05 (adult flag) on the thinnest path through schema, both registries, store, host, outlet, editor and page. Every later plan in this phase builds out from this slice.
Output: intimacy schema plugin with fixture, SCHEMA_REGISTRY and PLUGIN_REGISTRY entries, CharacterStore availableTypes/addPage/updatePage, PluginOutlet, SubDocHost, the Intimacy editor's context row, the page list with empty state and add button, and the UI integration spec.
</objective>

An effect calls `plugin().load()` and sets a private `editorType` signal; on rejection it logs `console.error('[PluginOutlet] failed to load', plugin().schema.type)` (never the data) and renders "This page couldn't be loaded." Template renders `<ng-container [ngComponentOutlet]="type" [ngComponentOutletInputs]="{ data: data(), mode: mode() }" />`. NgComponentOutlet has no output binding (RESEARCH Pitfall 5): read `viewChild(NgComponentOutlet)`, and in an effect subscribe to `componentInstance.dataChange` and re-emit on this component's `dataChange`. Unsubscribe in onCleanup, and skip re-subscribing when the instance is unchanged. If `componentInstance` is still undefined when the effect first runs, use `afterRenderEffect` instead.
